cleanup_scope: Only its own unreaped direct Popen child PID is signalled. Descendant probe attempts cleanup of its own direct child; no process-group kill or global scan.

accounting_note: Six fresh workers (three tests, three probes) are charged once each. Nested process CPU is not added. Initial shell inspection, source writing, report generation and packaging are outside these totals.
sampling_limit: Two matching inventories, even with required known live members, cannot exclude unregistered or short-lived descendants between enumeration/read instants; this is not a continuous physical-memory peak.
cleanup_limits: No guarantee of complete descendant cleanup under arbitrary faults: an ancestor can exhaust its per-layer grace and SIGKILL a child before that child finishes grandchild cleanup; a process stuck in the kernel may remain unreaped. Normal probe and bounded direct-child cleanup are the tested cases.
failed_probe_accounting: If a probe fails before producing its JSON, the outer worker receipt/log records the observed failure. Failed memory and complete descendant cost must remain unavailable when descendant reaping is incomplete; a wait4 receipt must not be promoted to all-descendant complete cost in that case.
